findings.title: Workflow result indexes obscure request-result coupling
findings.why_it_matters: The two repair workflows bind more than forty assertions and follow-up request factories to bare array offsets. Inserting, removing, or reordering one MCP request requires manually updating every dependent index; a missed update can make the smoke test inspect or mutate the wrong response while its error labels still describe the intended step.
findings.suggested_fix: Define descriptive step constants (or a keyed result map) beside each workflow and use them for both request factories and post-run assertions instead of literal results[n] offsets.
evidence: The process workflow's request list spans lines 934-1006, while its factories and assertions reference results[5], results[9], results[11]-results[13], and results[16]-results[22].
The collaboration workflow repeats the positional protocol on lines 1114-1175 and then references results[0], results[3]-results[13], and results[16]-results[23] across lines 1180-1305.
